I am 65 years old and have farmed this land in Quzhou for more than 40 years. I never went to school, but I know every plot by touch and smell. I have 8 mu of good flat land. I do not grow cotton or vegetables like some younger people — too much labor and the prices jump around. I stick to the wheat-maize rotation that my father did, and his father before him. It feeds my family and leaves some grain to sell.

My wheat is already in the ground from last autumn. I planted jimai22, an improved variety that does well here. Right now, at the start of the growing season, I need to topdress it with urea when it turns green, and irrigate it three times total — green-up, jointing, and heading. I always rotary-till before wheat planting to break up the soil. For fertilizer, I put down about 100 jin of compound fertilizer at planting, then another 50 jin of urea in spring. That gives the wheat what it needs. I also spray four times total: twice for insects, once for weeds, and once for fungus because the spring has been damp lately. I expect about 1000 jin per mu, same as most years.

After the wheat comes off in early June, I will immediately plant summer maize — denghai605, a hybrid seed from the shop that everyone trusts. I do not till for the maize; I drill straight into the wheat stubble to save time and fuel before the rains come. I apply about 100 jin of compound fertilizer at planting, and that is usually enough nitrogen for maize. I irrigate twice — once at planting if it is dry, and once at the trumpet stage. Maize gets three sprays: twice for insects and once for weeds. I do not bother with fungicide on maize. I expect around 1100 jin per mu.

This is my plan. It is not fancy, but it has never failed me.
